results.title: Holiday advertising spending 2026: sourced figures
results.markdown:
Title: Holiday advertising spending 2026: sourced figures

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/holiday-advertising-spending-2026

Published Time: 2026-10-17T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
The closest dated figures are retail forecasts and full-year ad estimates. The National Retail Federation forecasts $1.013 trillion in November and December retail sales, up 4.2%.

The IAB expects full-year 2026 US ad spend to rise 12.3%, and estimates digital video at $81.9 billion.

## 2026 holiday sales forecasts by publisher

These are forecasts of what shoppers will spend. They still set the size of the market your holiday ads compete for. Alongside the [NRF’s October 15 holiday forecast](https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/nrf-forecasts-2026-holiday-sales-growth-as-consumers-remain-resilient), several other publishers released their own numbers this fall.

![Image 1: Shoppers carrying bags past decorated storefronts on a small-town street at dusk in December](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/5586d87eb701daad95c042e6d621630cde386679bc4f60c4df87a3abfbe0f356.jpg)

| Publisher | Release date | Period covered | Scope | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| National Retail Federation (NRF) | Oct 15, 2026 | Nov 1 to Dec 31 | US retail, excluding auto dealers, gas stations and restaurants | $1.013 trillion, up 4.2% |
| Adobe, [reported by Drip](https://www.drip.com/blog/holiday-shopping-statistics) | September 2026 | Nov 1 to Dec 31 | US online sales | $275.1 billion, up 6.7%; Cyber Monday $15.1 billion |
| [Mastercard Economics Institute (SpendingPulse)](https://www.mastercard.com/us/en/news-and-trends/stories/2026/2026-holiday-shopping-forecast.html) | Sep 23, 2026 | Nov 1 to Dec 24 | US retail excluding autos and gas, in-store and online | Up 5.5% |
| Visa Business and Economic Insights | Nov 5, 2026 | November and December | US holiday retail sales | Up 4.5% |
| [Circana Holiday Purchase Intentions Study](https://www.circana.com/post/circana-s-2026-holiday-study-finds-consumers-spending-selectively-not-stepping-away) | Oct 8, 2026 | Fourth quarter | US, survey of 3,534 consumers | Down 1% to up 2.5%; average planned spend $779, versus $796 last year |
| Forrester, [cited by Digital Remedy](https://www.digitalremedy.com/blog/your-best-holiday-sales-happen-where-your-pixel-cant-reach/) | October 2026 | Holiday season | US retail | $1.1 trillion, up 5.1%; ecommerce up 11.6% |
| [Bain & Company holiday outlook](https://www.bain.com/insights/2026-holiday-shopping-outlook-infographic/) | 2026 | Holiday season | US, in-store plus nonstore | About $1,016 billion forecast (roughly $695 billion in-store, $321 billion nonstore) |
| [EMARKETER February forecast](https://www.emarketer.com/content/its-never-too-early-whats-ahead-2026-holiday-season) | February 2026 | Holiday season | US retail and ecommerce | Retail up about 2.6%, ecommerce up about 6.6% |

The totals differ mainly because each publisher draws the season and the category list differently. Mastercard stops on December 24 while NRF runs to December 31. Circana covers the full fourth quarter, and NRF leaves out restaurants, gas and car dealers, while Adobe counts only online sales. EMARKETER’s figure is from February, months older than the rest. Read each number against its own definition. Don’t average them into one consensus figure.

Search, social, and TV budgets get planned and reported annually, so the dated channel figures below cover all of 2026, not November and December alone. The table collects the latest US figures, as compiled by [Digital Applied from IAB and IAB/PwC reports](https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/digital-advertising-statistics-2026-data-points), plus EMARKETER’s retail media forecast.

| Channel | Figure | Period | Publisher | Release date | Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All media, US | Up 12.3% (raised from 9.5% in January) | 2026 | IAB Outlook Study, survey of 200+ brand and agency buyers | Sep 10, 2026 | Forecast |
| US digital video | $81.9 billion, up 11% | 2026 | IAB video report, based on Guideline data | 2026 | Estimate |
| Connected TV (CTV) | $29.3 billion (from $26.5 billion in 2025) | 2026 | IAB video report | 2026 | Estimate |
| Social video, including YouTube | $31.9 billion (from $28.2 billion in 2025) | 2026 | IAB video report | 2026 | Estimate |
| Linear TV | 39% of US TV and video ad spend, with digital video at 61% | 2026 | IAB video report | 2026 | Estimate |
| Retail media | $71.09 billion, up from $60.32 billion in 2025 | 2026 | [EMARKETER retail media forecast](https://www.emarketer.com/content/faq-on-holiday-marketing-how-marketers-win-longer-leaner-season) | 2026 | Forecast |
| US internet advertising, all formats | $294.6 billion, up 13.9% | 2025 | IAB/PwC Internet Advertising Revenue Report | Apr 16, 2026 | Reported revenue (industry estimate) |

Two things stand out. Social video passed CTV in 2025 and stays ahead in the 2026 estimate, so the sight, sound and motion budget is split across feeds and living-room screens. And the IAB’s all-media forecast rose during the year, which means buyers expected to spend more by September than they did in January. For background on the streaming side, see our explainer on [how OTT and streaming ads work](https://adwave.com/resources/what-is-ott-advertising).

None of these sources publishes a 2026 holiday-only figure for search. The 2025 IAB/PwC total is the only measured number in the table. Everything else is an estimate or forecast that will be revised. Spend totals also say nothing about price per impression. Our guide to [what CPM means for ad costs](https://adwave.com/resources/what-is-cpm-in-advertising) covers that side.

## What advertisers say about holiday TV and CTV budgets

The clearest signals on TV and CTV holiday budgets come from surveys, and each has its own method. Advertiser Perceptions, commissioned by Premion, which Tegna owns, surveyed agency and brand marketers who used streaming TV advertising in both 2025 and 2026, fielding the survey in October 2025. Nearly 70% of CTV advertisers said they expect to raise CTV spending in 2026, by an average of 17%, according to [Marketing Dive’s report on the Premion survey](https://www.marketingdive.com/news/how-brands-and-agencies-are-strategizing-ctv-investments-in-2026/815981/).

![Image 2: Family watching television together in a living room decorated for the holidays](https://media.wavefront.adwave-apps.com/ws/ws_adwave/b57cd5d8cf0fed114cf7090b4ab17fd67e0611e04a49785a6a862d0b93428f71.jpg)

tvScientific by Pinterest surveyed 487 US marketers in July 2026 for its [2026 Holiday & Seasonal Shopping Trends Report](https://www.tvscientific.com/2026-holiday-seasonal-shopping-report). The survey covered plans running from Labor Day and October Prime Day through Black Friday Cyber Monday and New Year’s. A separate tvScientific playbook aimed at enterprise marketers is [quoted by The Agile Brand](https://www.instagram.com/p/DdohVZ5DLr6/) as finding that 54% of marketers’ seasonal media budgets go to Performance TV and CTV combined. tvScientific sells Performance TV, so treat this as a vendor survey of larger advertisers. It doesn’t describe the whole market.

Both surveys are statements of intent, gathered months before the season. They show where buyers planned to move budget, not what they actually spent once the season played out. For household-level streaming context, see our [average streaming spending figures](https://adwave.com/resources/average-streaming-spending).

## Forecasts versus last season’s actuals

Last year’s forecasts ran ahead of the results. A year ago NRF predicted holiday sales growth of 3.7% to 4.2%. The final 2025 figure came in at $972 billion, up 3.1%, short of both the range and the $1 trillion mark, as [MarketingCharts’ holiday data hub](https://www.marketingcharts.com/industries/retail-and-e-commerce-239529) notes. NRF’s 2026 release confirms the 3.1% result. Adobe’s online number was closer to the mark: it measured 2025 online holiday sales at $257.8 billion, up 6.8%, according to Drip’s roundup of Adobe data.

Read the 2026 forecasts as a range of plausible outcomes rather than a single consensus number. The publishers at the optimistic end, Mastercard at 5.5% and Forrester at 5.1%, and Circana’s range, which includes a decline, are all describing the same season with different models and definitions. Online growth has been the more consistent part of the story in recent years. Set up [measuring whether your ads worked](https://adwave.com/resources/advertising-effectiveness-measurement) before your campaign starts so you have your own number rather than waiting on next year’s reports.

## What the numbers mean for a small advertiser’s holiday budget

The data points to an early start. In Circana’s October 2025 survey, 48% of consumers browsed before Thanksgiving and 44% planned to shop earlier overall, as listed in [Circana’s guide to preparing for holida

results.title: CTV Advertising in 2026: Updated Market Forecast
results.markdown:
Title: CTV Advertising in 2026: Updated Market Forecast

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/ctv-advertising-2026-update

Published Time: 2026-02-03T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
U.S. CTV advertising is projected to reach approximately $38 billion in 2026, according to [eMarketer's latest forecast](https://www.emarketer.com/content/us-tv-connected-tv-ad-spending-forecasts-h2-2025), continuing the double-digit growth that has defined the channel for the past five years. The market grew from $33.35 billion in 2025 to an expected $38 billion in 2026, representing roughly 14% year-over-year growth. By 2028, CTV is projected to reach $46.89 billion and surpass traditional TV advertising for the first time in history. For small businesses, this expansion creates unprecedented opportunity to reach audiences on the biggest screen in the house, with targeting precision and budget flexibility that traditional TV never offered.

*   $38B

Projected U.S. CTV ad spend (2026)

*   14%

Expected year-over-year growth

*   2028

Year CTV will surpass traditional TV

## What the data shows

The numbers paint a clear picture of CTV's acceleration and linear TV's structural decline.

### The 2026 forecast in context

CTV ad spending is projected to grow from $33.35 billion in 2025 to approximately $38 billion in 2026, according to [eMarketer](https://www.emarketer.com/content/4-ctv-ad-spend-trends-track-2025). This 14% growth rate, while slightly lower than 2024's 16%, still represents extraordinary expansion for a major advertising channel. For comparison, total U.S. advertising grows at roughly 5-7% annually. CTV is growing at twice that pace or more.

The multi-year trajectory shows sustained momentum:

*   **2024:** $28.6 billion (actual)

*   **2025:** $33.35 billion (16% growth)

*   **2026:** ~$38 billion (14% projected growth)

*   **2027:** ~$42 billion (11% projected growth)

*   **2028:** $46.89 billion ([eMarketer](https://www.emarketer.com/content/us-tv-connected-tv-ad-spending-forecasts-h2-2025))

*   **2029:** ~$51 billion

Even as growth moderates toward 11% annually by 2029, CTV will add nearly $20 billion in U.S. ad dollars over the next four years. The market isn't just growing. It's compounding at rates that dwarf traditional media.

### The crossover point

The most significant milestone in the forecast: [eMarketer projects](https://www.emarketer.com/content/ctv-becomes-tv-s-growth-engine-linear-collapses) CTV ad spending will surpass traditional TV ad spending for the first time in 2028. At that point, CTV is expected to reach $46.89 billion while traditional TV advertising falls to approximately $45 billion.

This crossover represents more than a statistical milestone. It marks the definitive shift of television advertising from broadcast and cable to streaming. Linear TV has already fallen to approximately 12% of global ad spending, according to [WARC Media](https://www.warc.com/), while CTV is on pace to exceed 40% of video ad spending by 2030.

### What's driving the forecast

Several structural factors support continued CTV growth through 2026 and beyond:

**Ad-supported tier maturation:** Netflix's ad tier revenue exceeded $1.5 billion in 2025 and is [expected to double in 2026](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/21/netflix-advertising-revenue-strategy-paying-off.html). Disney+ continues expanding its 157 million ad-supported viewers. Amazon Prime Video's ad tier, launched in January 2024, now reaches the vast majority of Prime subscribers. These platforms are still in early innings of ad monetization.

**Viewership momentum:** Streaming captured a record 47.5% of all U.S. TV viewing in December 2025, according to [Nielsen](https://www.nielsen.com/data-center/the-gauge/). Each percentage point of viewing share that shifts from linear to streaming represents billions in advertising opportunity.

**Measurement improvements:** AI-driven personalization is projected to power 80% of CTV ads by 2027, according to industry forecasts. Better measurement drives advertiser confidence, which drives spend.

**Retail media integration:** Retail media CTV ad sales are expected to grow from $4.99 billion in 2025 to $10.28 billion by 2028, more than doubling as commerce data connects with TV advertising.

## Breaking down the numbers

Understanding the components of the 2026 forecast helps advertisers plan their strategies.

The CTV market remains fragmented, with only three companies expected to capture more than 10% of ad sales in 2026:

**YouTube:** Nearly 12% market share, approximately $9.21 billion in net CTV ad sales. YouTube continues to dominate as the single largest streaming destination, capturing over 12% of all TV viewing.

**Amazon:** Over 10% market share through Prime Video (with its massive ad-supported base), Fire TV, Twitch, and Freevee. Amazon's commerce data creates unique attribution advantages for advertisers.

**Disney:** Over 10% market share combining Hulu (the largest single ad-revenue streaming service at $4 billion+), Disney+ (growing to ~$1.5 billion), and ESPN. The Hulu-Disney+ integration in 2026 could push combined annual ad revenues past $5 billion.

**Netflix:** The fastest-growing major platform, with ad revenue expected to more than double from $1.5 billion in 2025. Netflix's premium content and 94 million ad-tier users make it increasingly attractive to advertisers.

**Others:** Peacock, Paramount+, Max, Tubi, Pluto TV, and The Roku Channel divide the remaining market share. FAST services collectively represent the fastest-growing segment.

The 2026 forecast encompasses multiple advertising formats:

**Standard video ads:** 15-30 second spots remain the dominant format, with completion rates exceeding 95% on streaming platforms.

**Interactive and shoppable ads:** Growing from a small base, with retail media integrations enabling direct purchase from TV ads.

**Pause screen ads:** Static ads shown when viewers pause content, a native streaming format gaining traction.

**AI-personalized creative:** Dynamic ads tailored to viewer context, projected to represent 80% of CTV ads by 2027.

### By buying method

Programmatic purchasing continues gaining share:

*   **Programmatic guaranteed:** ~38% of 2026 spend

*   **Private marketplace (PMP):** ~32% of spend

*   **Open exchange:** ~18% of spend

*   **Direct/IO:** ~12% of spend (declining)

The shift toward programmatic benefits smaller advertisers. When 88% of inventory is available through automated systems, barriers to entry drop dramatically.

## Why it matters for your business

The 2026 CTV forecast isn't just an industry statistic. It represents a fundamental shift in how businesses of all sizes can reach customers.

### The economics favor small businesses

Traditional TV advertising operated on a simple principle: big reach required big budgets. A local business wanting to advertise on television faced minimum spends of tens of thousands of dollars, plus production costs that could easily add another $50,000 or more. The economics simply didn't work for most small businesses.

CTV changes that equation entirely:

**Programmatic buying enables any budget level.** The same infrastructure handling $38 billion in spend serves campaigns starting at $50.

**Geographic targeting eliminates waste.** A local restaurant doesn't pay to reach viewers three states away. A dental practice targets only households in its service area.

**AI creative tools eliminate production barriers.** What once required $50,000 in production now costs nothing with platforms like [Adwave](https://adwave.com/) that generate professional commercials from your website.

The growth to $38 billion in 2026 means more inventory becoming available on more platforms at more accessible price points. As the market scales, competition among platforms drives innovation in targeting, measurement, and advertiser tools. Small businesses benefit from infrastructure originally built for enterprise advertisers.

### The trust factor

Television remains the most trusted advertising medium among consumers. Viewers expect advertising on TV in ways they don't on social media or display. The premium environment of streaming, with professional content and intentional viewing, creates receptive audiences for brand messages. When a local business appears on the same screen as national brands, it gains implicit credibility.

### The timing opportunity

The trajectory toward $38 billion in 2026 means the market is maturing but still growing rapidly. Businesses that establish streaming TV presence now, while inventory is abundant and competition among small advertisers is still developing, will have advantages over latecomers:

*   Build institutional knowledge through testing

*   Develop creative assets that resonate

*   Establish measurement frameworks

*   Claim share of voice before competitors

## How to take advantage of this trend

Acting on the 2026 CTV forecast requires a practical appro
